feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. The controller is the iteration 6 controller unchanged, so the race isolates the track change. Evidence from earlier races: iteration 6 (70.83, best) had one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error 0.0641 and 0.0669 m and steering_oscillation of 0.133 and 0.148. Iterations 7 and 8 closed the footprint and span levers at 12 mm (8 mm gave 67.75; ±0.04 m gave 36.6, with s-bend progress collapsing to 0.04). Iteration 5 showed that body_length 0.12 m lowers the score, and iteration 3 showed that the forward offset y 0.07 m does not remove the loss. Mass is at its 0.4 kg floor. Track width is the remaining single lever. Note that turn rate scales with 1/wheel_track, so 0.14 m gives about 14 percent less turn per unit of PWM. Read the next race by these branches. If line losses fall below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom and steering_oscillation falls, turn rate was the limit, so try wheel_track 0.16 m next. If line losses stay at 1.0 and progress is unchanged, the controller rather than the geometry is limiting the robot, so return to wheel_track 0.12 m as the base. If line losses rise or the oval score falls, the robot is under-turning, so return to 0.12 m.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events fall below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom and steering_oscillation falls below 0.133 and 0.148 (iteration 6), try wheel_track 0.16 m with the other fields unchanged, to test whether more damping still helps.

If line losses stay at 1.0 per run with progress and score unchanged, return wheel_track to 0.12 m and hold the iteration 6 geometry as the final base, since no geometry lever has yet beaten 70.83 at 12 mm footprints with ±0.03 m span (iterations 6 to 8).

If line_loss_events rise above 1.0 or the score falls below 70.83 with progress on the s-bend lower, return to wheel_track 0.12 m, since the slower turn rate is causing the robot to under-turn the sharpest bends (iteration 6 evidence).
